recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | Corven — Cloud Development Platform for the CKB Ecosystem
recent_posts.author: xingtianchunyan
recent_posts.content_text:
Hi @lestonEth, thanks for submitting the Corven — Cloud Development Platform for the CKB Ecosystem proposal.
Before we move to committee review, I’d like to share some personal pre-review feedback (not a committee decision) to help strengthen your proposal:
1. Format & Completeness (checked against the official proposal template):
Required Funding & Funding Breakdown: Missing the required sub-headings “A. Required Funding” and “B. Funding Breakdown”. The explanation for exceeding $1,000 is too brief; a detailed justification is needed.
Deliverables + How to Verify: Deliverables listed without specific acceptance criteria. Verification steps lack expected outputs, environment requirements, and cost control notes.
2. Funding Standards:
Project type: Pure technical (Developer Tool). Requested $2,000 exceeds the standard cap of $1,000. The brief justification is insufficient. Recommendation: reduce to $1,000 or below with a scaled scope, or provide a detailed argument for a special/high-difficulty tier (requires full committee consensus). Also, the weekly budget ($600/$600/$500/$300) does not match the category breakdown ($700/$500/$350/$150/$300), causing confusion.
3. Content Logic:
The 4-week timeline for a solo developer to reach production-ready MVP is optimistic; testing and documentation may be compromised.
Verification steps need more detail: expected outputs (e.g., compilation success message), browser requirements, login needs.
Open-source license not specified (required by Spark Program).
Suggestions:
Adjust the budget to $1,000 or less and trim scope accordingly, or add a thorough justification for a higher amount.
Revise §8 with clear acceptance criteria for each deliverable and concrete verification steps (expected outputs, environment).
Align the weekly budget with the category breakdown or explain the relationship.
Extend the timeline to 6-8 weeks or reduce scope to ensure quality.
Specify an open-source license (e.g., MIT).
Please revise and reply in this thread. Looking forward to the updated version!
Best,
xingtian

recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | CKB Wallet Behaviour Intelligence
recent_posts.author: mulinya
recent_posts.content_text:
Hello xingtianchunyan,
Apologies for the miscommunication and for missing the recent progress update due to unavoidable circumstances.
I have been primarily focused on data collection. Since open bot wallets datasets on CKB arent available I built a local CKB bot transaction simulator that generates ground-truth labeled behavioral data on a local CKB devnet. The simulator communicates directly with the CKB JSON-RPC using a lightweight Python transaction-construction package that i built, implements transaction signing in pure Python, runs concurrent bot simulations, and records every confirmed transaction into a labeled dataset for downstream behavioral analysis and model training.
This work currently lives in a separate repository as supporting infrastructure and will be merged into the main Wallet Behaviour Intelligence (GitHub - FadhilMulinya/ckb-intel · GitHub) upon completion as part of the community deliverables.
The generated datasets are available here:
https://github.com/FadhilMulinya/intel-synthetic/tree/main/data
So far, I’ve completed simulations with 300 bots and 500 bots , generating approximately 180,000+ devnet transactions. A detailed analysis of this dataset will be included in next week’s update.
The model will be trained using a combination of CKB mainnet, testnet, and devnet data. In parallel, I have been collecting human wallet data from mainnet and testnet by scapping the respective networks using some python scripts. However, most publicly discoverable wallets are exchange or service wallets rather than representative individual users but still looking for various ways to get sufficient data.
Work related to training the machine learning model has already commenced, and I’ll provide a detailed update on the training pipeline, feature engineering, and initial evaluation results in next week’s progress report.
Once again, I apologize for the miscommunication. If anything affects the reporting schedule in the future, I’ll make sure to communicate it promptly. Thank you for your patience and understanding.

recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | Fiber Submarine Swap Service
recent_posts.author: xingtianchunyan
recent_posts.content_text:
Hi @George_Liam,
thanks for submitting the Fiber Submarine Swap Service proposal.
Before we move to committee review, I’d like to share some personal pre-review feedback (not a committee decision) to help strengthen your proposal:
1. Format & Completeness (checked against the official proposal template):
Project Overview: Missing a clear project type (e.g., DApp, developer tool, etc.).
Team Profile: Lacks core member names/roles, verifiable links (GitHub/LinkedIn), and contact info.
Technical Approach: No tech stack specified, no architecture diagram, and PTLC implementation details are insufficient.
To-Do List: Weekly goals are too vague; template requires concrete tasks per week.
Funding Breakdown: Needs a more detailed breakdown (by week or category) to justify the $800 allocation.
Deliverables & Verification: Missing a list of deliverables with acceptance criteria.
Current State vs Funded Work: Entirely absent; please clarify what has already been built.
CKB Alignment: Lacks concrete design details (e.g., how Cell Model or CKB scripts are used).
2. Funding Standards:
The proposal is a pure technical project, and the requested $1,000 is within the standard cap. However, the budget breakdown is too coarse; a more granular breakdown (e.g., per week or per resource) would strengthen the justification.
3. Content Logic:
Strong points: The problem (inbound liquidity for Fiber users) is real and well-articulated, and the verification plan is excellent—multiple low-cost, reproducible methods. The first-week research milestone is a smart risk mitigator.
Concerns: The team’s credibility is unverifiable due to missing identity and background info. The technical approach lacks critical details (PTLC implementation, tech stack), making feasibility hard to assess. The absence of a “current state” section raises uncertainty about whether the project starts from scratch, which could strain the 6-week timeline.
Suggestions:
Provide core team members’ names/roles, verifiable GitHub/LinkedIn links, and a Discord/email contact.
Add a “Current State vs Funded Work” section describing any existing code, research, or prototypes.
Expand the Technical Approach with a clear tech stack, an architecture diagram, and more specifics on PTLC locking.
Break down the $800 budget into weekly or category-based items (e.g., development hours, testing, documentation).
List deliverables explicitly in §8 with verification criteria.
Please revise and reply in this thread. Looking forward to the updated version!
Best,
xingtian

recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | Fiber RGB++ Swap
recent_posts.author: xingtianchunyan
recent_posts.content_text:
Hi @Carl ,
Thank you for your continued interest in the Spark Program.
After review by the Spark Program committee, your proposal has been assigned a status of Pending. This is not a rejection, but an invitation to revise.
The committee recognizes the value of connecting RGB++ assets with Fiber’s instant-settlement layer, and we appreciate your clear identification of the current limitation in CCH. However, the proposal lacks sufficient detail to demonstrate that the project can achieve its stated goals within the proposed timeline and budget.
Main Revision Recommendations:
Clarify deliverables and verification criteria:
The current proposal does not provide specific and verifiable deliverables for each milestone. Please list a clear set of deliverables (the list should specify the format of each deliverable) based on the template (Spark Program: Mini-Grant Initiative - #7 by xingtianchunyan) and map them to each milestone; Additionally, define objectively measurable verification methods and success criteria for each deliverable, including how to test the correctness of atomic exchanges, how to handle edge cases, and how to ensure security, so that the committee can objectively evaluate progress.
Please revise and resubmit based on the feedback above. We will arrange a new round of review as soon as possible.
Best,
xingtian
On behalf of the Spark Program Committee

recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | Cell Sandbox — A Visual Playground for the CKB Cell Model
recent_posts.author: zynor
recent_posts.content_text:
Hi everyone,
This week I focused on improving the Cell Sandbox wallet flow, Build Tx experience, and alignment with current CKB documentation.
Live demo:
https://cell-sandbox-m.vercel.app/
Repository:
https://github.com/zynorr/cell-sandbox
Commits:
Wallet, transaction flow, and CKB accuracy updates
README and fresh screenshots
What I Worked On
Added the CCC wallet selector with JoyID, MetaMask, OKX Wallet, UniSat, and UTXO Global.
Clarified that designed Cells are local drafts until marked as transaction outputs.
Improved Build Tx to show wallet-selected inputs, fees calculated during signing, and change returned to the wallet.
Added stricter validation and separated lock-script and type-script presets.
Updated CKB terminology across Learn, Design, Inspect, and Build.
Made CKB Transfer and fresh DAO Deposit buildable.
Marked xUDT, Spore, Omnilock, and Always Success as design-only.
Corrected DAO data and cell dependencies, xUDT amount decoding, and Spore Molecule decoding.
Transaction Inspector
The inspector now resolves previous input Cells, recognizes cellbase inputs, handles DAO capacity exceptions, and uses exact capacity and fee calculations. It also includes reproducible cellbase and multi-input Pudge examples.
Documentation
I rewrote the README and added fresh screenshots for Learn, Design Cells, Inspect Tx, and Build Tx.
Verification
The current version passes TypeScript, ESLint, 104 Vitest tests, the Next.js production build, wallet selector testing, and a manual Learn-to-Build walkthrough.
I would appreciate feedback on whether the transition from designing a Cell to marking it as an output is clear, and whether wallet funding and design-only templates are explained well enough.
Next, I plan to test another complete signed Pudge transaction and continue refining mobile and wallet error states.

recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | CKB Appchain Kit MVP
recent_posts.author: xingtianchunyan
recent_posts.content_text:
Hi @Cipher_Kage ,
Thank you for submitting your proposal to the Spark Program.
The committee has completed its review and, after careful discussion, regrets to Reject the CKB Appchain Kit MVP proposal at this time.
We want to be transparent about the reasoning behind this decision:
Unaddressed Core Technical Challenges:
The proposal aims to build an Appchain Kit, but it does not clearly articulate how the fundamental technical challenges of a CKB-anchored appchain will be solved. Issues such as the security model (rollup vs. validium), data availability, state verification mechanisms (fraud proofs or validity proofs), checkpoint finality, and the overall trust model are critical. Without specific solutions or a clear technical roadmap for these core problems, the committee cannot evaluate the project’s feasibility and long-term value to the ecosystem.
We appreciate the work your team has put into researching and conceptualizing this tool. Keep building, and feel free to reach out anytime if you have questions or want to discuss alternative directions!
Best,
xingtian
On behalf of the Spark Program Committee

recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | Fiber Network Payment Gateway for WooCommerce
recent_posts.author: xingtianchunyan
recent_posts.content_text:
Hi @Oracle,
Thank you for your interest in the Spark Program.
The committee has completed its review and, after careful discussion, regrets to Reject the Fiber Network Payment Gateway for WooCommerce proposal at this time.
We want to be transparent about the reasoning behind this decision:
Platform compliance uncertainty:
We have encountered situations where projects in the ecosystem ultimately could not be listed on platforms like Shopify due to policy and compliance requirements. Similarly, a WooCommerce payment plugin must pass review by the WooCommerce official marketplace, and that review may impose requirements that are currently outside the project’s scope. This can result in the plugin never being distributed to the target users.
Ecosystem readiness and value circulation concerns:
While we recognize the technical merit of your proposal, the committee has observed a large number of Fiber‑based payment and exchange projects that focus on value circulation without concrete value creation. We prefer to see more production‑side and consumption‑side applications built on Fiber. At this stage, a payment gateway for WooCommerce risks becoming another “empty circulation” tool without a critical mass of merchants and consumers actively using Fiber.
We appreciate the work your team has put into this project. If you plan to participate directly in the Fiber ecosystem in the future by developing projects for both the production and consumer sides, we welcome you to submit a new application.
Keep building, and feel free to reach out anytime!
Best,
xingtian
On behalf of the Spark Program Committee

recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | ckb-joyid-failure-explainer
recent_posts.author: xingtianchunyan
recent_posts.content_text:
Hi @Crackdevs ,
Thank you for your interest in the Spark Program.
The committee has completed its review and, after careful discussion, regrets to reject the ckb-joyid-failure-explainer project at this time.
We want to be transparent about the reasoning behind this decision:
Unclear usage scenario and workflow / Immature tool design:
The committee feels the developer has not fully considered the complete usage scenario and workflow for this tool. The design is not yet mature enough compared to the existing debugging patterns in the ecosystem. We strongly recommend reviewing the official CKB script error codes (GitHub - nervosnetwork/ckb-script-error-codes: This is a wiki to collect documentations about error codes returned by various ckb scripts. · GitHub) to understand how errors are currently structured and surfaced, as this tool’s intended functionality might overlap or conflict with existing standards.
Lack of clear community demand:
Currently, there is no clearly expressed demand within the CKB developer community for a dedicated CLI tool to parse JoyID/CCC failure artifacts. The debugging workflow for these specific integrations is still evolving, and a standalone explainer tool is premature without a demonstrated user base.
We appreciate the work your team has put into researching this area and drafting the proposal. Keep building, and feel free to reach out anytime!
Best,
xingtian
On behalf of the Spark Program Committee

recent_posts.author: xingtianchunyan
recent_posts.content_text:
Hi @Gabriel_Temsten ,
Thank you for taking the time to revise the proposal based on our earlier feedback. The committee has completed its review and, after careful discussion, regrets to Reject the Spore Metadata Standard and Reference Validator at this time.
We want to be transparent about the reasoning behind this decision:
Time and scope are not yet mature:
The current Spore specification maintenance is still relatively disorganized and needs further optimization and maturation. At this stage, simply formatting the existing specifications does not provide meaningful value to the ecosystem. The committee believes the effort would be better spent once the underlying standards have stabilized.
We appreciate your interest and encourage you to revisit this idea once the Spore specification landscape has become more mature. Keep building, and feel free to reach out anytime!
Best,
